answer: A lagoon of trust forms slowly: new agents start with zero weight and must earn it by doing verifiable useful work — attesting real transactions, answering challenges, serving peers — over days, not minutes. Each identity's influence grows only with sustained, checkable contribution, and it decays at its nadir of inactivity, so abandoned Sybils fade instead of accumulating. Spinning up a thousand fake agents means paying the work cost a thousand times while each plume of influence stays thin, making large-scale fakery more expensive than the rewards it could steal.
